messages.subject: Trouble with aggregation
parts:
Dear all,

We are trying to process our accelerometer data with GGIR. However, our aggregation process does not produce any results. We were hoping that GGIR would give us each minute per day per participant that we can manually merge it to every quarter hour per day.

For the processing we were using the following code:

GGIR::GGIR(

  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),

  datadir="~/Actigraph/actigraph_processing/data-raw",

  outputdir="~/Actigraph/actigraph_processing/output-data",

  do.report=c(2,4,5),

  #=====================

  # Part 2

  #=====================

  strategy = 1,

  hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,

  maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,

  qwindow=c(0,24),

  mvpathreshold =c(100),

  bout.metric = 6,

  excludefirstlast = FALSE,

  includenightcrit = 16,

  #=====================

  # Part 3 + 4

  #=====================

  def.noc.sleep = 1,

  outliers.only = TRUE,

  criterror = 4,

  do.visual = TRUE,

  #=====================

  # Part 5

  #=====================

  threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),

  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,

  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),

  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),

  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,

  #=====================

  # Visual report

  #=====================

  timewindow = c("WW"),

  visualreport=TRUE)

 

The processing was successful, so we wanted to exclude the participants by using the personsummary part 2/5, daysummary part2 and time series. Fortunately, the three summaries are outputs of the processing but we still need the time series.

We already tried to use the parameter " part5_agg2_60seconds=TRUE ", but it didn't work:

 

GGIR::GGIR(

    mode = c(1,2,3,4,5),

    datadir = here::here("data-raw"),

    outputdir = here::here("output-timeseries"),

    do.report = c(2,4,5),

    do.parallel = TRUE,

    #=====================

    # Part 2

    #=====================

    strategy = 1,

    hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,

    maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,

    qwindow=c(0,24),

    mvpathreshold =c(100),

    bout.metric = 6,

    excludefirstlast = FALSE,

    includenightcrit = 16,

    #=====================

    # Part 3 + 4

    #=====================

    def.noc.sleep = 1,

    outliers.only = TRUE,

    criterror = 4,

    do.visual = TRUE,

    #=====================

    # Part 5

    #=====================

    threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),

    boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,

    boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),

    boutdur.mvpa = c(1),

    includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,

    part5_agg2_60seconds=TRUE,

    #=====================

    # Visual report

    #=====================

    timewindow = c("WW"),

    visualreport=TRUE)


Any help/tips would be greatly appreciated.

Looking forward to hearing from you and thank you in advance.

Sincerely,


Elif

messages.subject: Re: Trouble with aggregation
parts:
Hi Elif, 

If you want epoch level data you need to use epochvalues2csv = TRUE, which generates a csv folder in the meta folder per participant. This is a csv version of part of the basic meta file you already have. If you open any file in the output_study/meta/basic folder and look at M$metashort you will see the same info.  

Looks like you have used default windowsizes which are 5s epochs, so you may need to specify windowsizes = c(60,900,3600) to generate your intended minute-level data, just be aware this will alter the results in the summary outputs as it's a completely different parameter for processing all the data. 

@Vincent maybe we need something like a epochvalues2csv_agg2_60seconds = TRUE or equivalent which only aggregates the csv, not the actual file reports? Or is there another way to do this that I'm not aware of?

Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Trouble with aggregation
parts:
Hi Elif and Ben,

This information is all stored inside the meta/ms2.out RData files. I only implemented the functionality epochvalues2csv = TRUE for those with limited R skills.

A better solution may be to document the format of those files and provide some guidance on how to use those files. That said, it took me under 5 minutes to write the following code which essentially derives the time series you are looking for:

# Load content of RData file from meta/ms2.out folder is loaded in R.
load("output_test/meta/ms2.out/01_left wrist_012345_2000-01-01 12-45-78.bin.RData")

# Convert timestamp to POSIX for convenience
tsFormat = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"
tz = ""
IMP$metashort$timestampPOSIX = as.POSIXlt(IMP$metashort$timestamp, format = tsFormat, tz = tz)

# Interpolate scores as they are in a different resolution
shortEpochLength = IMP$windowsizes[1]
longEpochLength = IMP$windowsizes[2]
NlongInsideShort = longEpochLength / shortEpochLength
scores = IMP$rout[rep(1:nrow(IMP$rout), each = NlongInsideShort),]

# Add column names to clarify what is what
colnames(scores) = c("nonwear", "clipping", "additonal_nonwear", "studyprotocol", "all")

# Now combine the scores with the epoch level timeseries
IMP$metashort = cbind(IMP$metashort, scores)

# IMP$metashort now be stored or used for your own R project work
write.csv(x = IMP$metashort, file = "myfile.csv", row.names = FALSE)


Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Trouble with aggregation
parts:
... and to aggregate it to minute level you could for example do:

# drop character timestamp
IMP$metashort = IMP$metashort[, -which(colnames(IMP$metashort) == "timestamp")]
#aggregate timestamps to minute level
IMP$metashort$timestamp_num = round(as.numeric(IMP$metashort$timestampPOSIX) / 60) * 60
# aggregate to minunte
perminute = aggregate(by = list(IMP$metashort$timestamp_num),x = IMP$metashort, FUN = mean)

However, I hope that GGIR itself already facilitates all the essential things you may want to do with the time series. If not, then please let me know. Sometimes it is more efficient to add something to GGIR then to have everyone develop their own local version of the exact same processing steps.

Cheers,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
